title: The invoice splits parts cost between the line's category and cost of goods
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure AccountingHub is enabled for the organization and the test location has no QuickBooks Online connection.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, in status Complete, billable, with line 1 billable with one stock part costing $30.00 and line 2 marked No Charge under Goodwill with one stock part costing $40.00.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Create invoice.
  3. Open Accounting > Journal Entries.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The invoice is created.

Step 3:

  • $30.00 posts to the parts cost of goods sold account mapped on Account Mappings.
  • $40.00 posts to 6430 Warranty & Goodwill Expense with the source "No Charge line".
  • The revenue is one entry and each part's cost is its own entry.
  • Each cost entry's memo carries work order 1's number, the category and, for line 2, the line number.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11765 (Story 8, AccountingHub, the closed work order and its parts cost), story SV-12226 (Story 12, A no-charge line on a billable work order)

  • S8-R7: “An invoice of a billable work order with no-charge lines (Story 12) reaches the hub as an ordinary invoice record with its revenue and receivable on the billable lines. The record carries a "No Charge lines" block: line number and title, category, original work order and line, original technician, hours, parts cost, expense account. The posting splits the parts cost: billable lines to the parts cost of goods sold account as today, each no-charge line to its category's mapping row (S6-R1). When a no-charge line's category row is empty, the invoice, its revenue and its receivable post at once and only that line's cost entries are held, with the reason "No Charge: [Category] row not mapped", until the row is mapped (S8-N2); a reversal that withdraws them marks them Dismissed (S4-R3). In Journal Entries the source of a no-charge line's entry reads "No Charge line".”
  • S12-R8: “Posting at invoice creation follows S7-R8 (QuickBooks) and S8-R7 (AccountingHub): the no-charge line's parts cost to its category's account, the rest as today. Invoice reversal reverses the whole invoice, no-charge entries included, and the lines keep their No Charge mark on the reopened work order.”

From: "Internal Work Orders technical implementation plan", 2026-10-28, last updated 2026-11-10 (revision 5, built on PRD v1.0), sources/TECH-PLAN-Internal-Work-Orders-upload-2026-11-12.md, read 12 Nov 2026

  • Tech plan line 3878 (TP-557): “Design frame 5/3c draws a billable invoice's revenue and parts cost as one entry (INV-7731). The hub produces separate entries: the invoice's revenue entry, plus one cost entry per part.”
  • Tech plan line 4342 (TP-585): “Family entries also append the category, and the line number when”
  • Tech plan line 4342 (TP-585): “so the ledger drill-down answers "which job, which category".”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
